budget_philosophy: R5 hard stop when evidence bottleneck dominates; at most 20, no obligation

data.source: User uploaded cleaned Columbia Speed Dating parquet
data.mixmosa: Already explored original GitHub CSV; no raw individual sharing
data.eligibility: restrict actor sex, dates with age and discipline nonmissing, retain observed chooser-target-event opportunity edges

scientific_context.novelty_gate: Results exploratory; N2/N3 impossible without independent untouched confirmation
scientific_context.previous_age_reversal_1_3: Not automatically recounted; challenge it with stronger controls
scientific_context.prior_models: Actor fixed effect alone gave within R2 popularity 0.139-0.163 vs similarity 0.005-0.011, but popularity calculated from contemporaneous other interactions and not ex ante.
scientific_context.drift: D0.5 within same mate selection science

procedures.pre_selection: Hypotheses and fixed checks committed before calculating new results
procedures.matched_data_proxy: Only other votes (not focal), not objective social value
procedures.binary_choice: yes/no each directed speed date, no pair formation

cycles.question: Can 2-way FE be identified from the graph and are wave/age/discipline and participant IDs coherent?
cycles.test: Inspect chooser-target bipartite connectivity per gender, feasibility and missingness; report number of unique actors, targets, repeat exposure; test no leakage via mirror outcomes; >=500 complete observations to fit.

cycles.question: Does absolute age resemblance survive actor AND target fixed effects?
cycles.test: Within graph, fit chooser+target FE linear-probability model with abs(age_target-age_chooser), signed gap, same field, standardized exogenous predictors. Candidate popularity is collinear with candidate FE and is NOT simultaneously entered. Compare actor FE versus two-way FE; report estimates and cluster chooser SE (descriptive).

cycles.question: Can a flexible target-age preference explain previously claimed age homophily?
cycles.test: Add target age quadratic and signed age gap; note target-age linear is collinear with target FE when ages constant. Use competing versions: actor FE + target-age and age gap; two-way FE + abs-age and signed-age (linear signed gap unidentifiable under both FE if ages constant). Detect collinearity via norm residualization, do NOT report invalid coefficients.

cycles.question: Does same-field academic signal survive two-way FE?
cycles.test: Estimate full chooser+candidate FE with same-field indicator and abs-age gap; estimate cluster-chooser SE, report coefficient and condition checks, compare actor-only model with same complete-case sample.

cycles.question: Can preserving both sides' observed yes-degrees within wave explain apparent age and field homophily?
cycles.test: Construct bipartite binary approval network within wave for each chooser sex; MCMC 2x2 checkerboard edge swaps preserving chooser/target yes-degree and observed opportunity graph. ≥200 saved samples after fixed burn-in, report successful swaps, mixing diagnostics; if insufficient acceptance/mixing mark INVALID_OR_BLOCKED, do not claim a p-value.

cycles.question: Does chooser and candidate effect heterogeneity account for popularity explanatory power?
cycles.test: Compare actor-FE R2 and two-way-FE baseline R2 within the same complete-case data; candidate FE is saturating popularity, compare fit not causal effect. Report number of parameters / model fit penalty.

cycles.question: Is the age reversal 1/3 robust to flexible age specification?
cycles.test: Compare Columbia age closeness vs chooser-normalized signed age; check within-wave sex patterns with leave-one-wave-out. If no Mixmosa person-level available, use existing stored Mixmosa aggregates and classify independent test BLOCKED.

cycles.question: Can a held-out event support prospective ranking mechanism?
cycles.test: Event-wise CV: predictors popularity of targets learned from other events only. If >95% actors unique to one event, gate BLOCKED; do not leak within test event. Record coverage.

cycles.question: Is the earlier 1/3 N46 grade robust or overstates novelty?
cycles.test: Adversarial review of prior art, sign reversal with signed age and event effects; downgrade if not uniquely supported; do not double count.

cycles.question: What independent data would discriminate popularity preference vs homophily under equal exposure?
cycles.test: Define prospective field study and design ethical/public-observable outcome; no fictional execution. R5 decision on further cycles.

remaining_slots_if_early_stop: N57-N66 unstarted and unspent; no automatic cycle claims
AB_requirements: Each completed loop A-J, revise CT2 after each, N1 dedup and ethics/privacy; freeze code SHA before running; only aggregate outputs uploaded
output: REPORT.md, LEDGER.json, RESULTS.json, CT2.svg, scripts/hashes and reproducibility bundle
